articles.headline: NFL Week 8's best arrivals, led by Rams' Quentin Lake
articles.description: Here's a look at the best-dressed players around the NFL in Week 8.
articles.headlineJa: NFL第8週のベスト・アライバル、ラムズのクエンティン・レイクがリード
articles.descriptionJa: NFL第8週で最もスタイリッシュだった選手たちを紹介します。
articles.body:
On the afternoon following Halloween, Los Angeles Rams defensive back Quentin Lake decided to rock a fit adopting a look simulating Neo from "The Matrix."

 

Lake's all-black look is one of the best fits of the season regardless of the costume theme. But the question is: does Lake prefer to take the red pill or the blue pill?

The long-flowing trench coat is the star of this fit, but I love the commitment to the bit with black-tinted sunglasses and black combat boots supporting the look.

It's always a perfect reminder of fall hitting warm-weather states like California allowing players to be more versatile with their looks.

Secondary shoutout to Lake's teammate -- Rams receiver Puka Nacua -- who also went with a trench coat vibe, except his is layered with an inner black leather jacket with overlapping lapel from luxury brand Umit Benan.

The Rams trench coat duo sets the standard for Week 8's best gameday tunnel fits. Here are more top Week 8 fits that caught our eye:

Monday night drip

The Chicago Bears' wide receiver room arrived in unison ahead of "Monday Night Football" against the Seattle Seahawks. The group rocked suits, something orchestrated by wide receivers and assistant head coach Antwaan Randle El. The Seahawks had their fair share of ties, too, including from wide receivers Tory Horton and Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

Sunday's best

Facing the Philadelphia Eagles on "Sunday Night Football," Washington Commanders wide receiver Stefon Diggs had some Philly inspiration for his look. He donned Philadelphia 76ers legend Allen Iverson's jersey in a clean fit.

Along with the Rams showing their versatility this week, Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce came dripped out in the earth tones and a leather jacket.

Minnesota Vikings' quarterback Kyler Murray and wide receiver Justin Jefferson reported to their duties in similar monochromatic looks, with Murray styling a double-breasted look with a white tank and a beanie to match.

Thursday night fashion

Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young opted for a clean Louis Vuitton shirt with a heavy jacket on top and sleek sunglasses. On the other side, Green Bay Packers safety Javon Bullard went with a denim tie shirt from the clothing brand Jagne.

articles.headline: Coby White returns for Hornets, Kon Knueppel 'right around the corner'
articles.description: Coby White made his season debut for the Hornets on Monday vs. the Pistons and second-year guard Kon Kneuppel's return is also expected soon.
articles.headlineJa: コービー・ホワイトがホーネッツに復帰、コン・クニュペルも「復帰間近」
articles.descriptionJa: コービー・ホワイトが月曜日のピストンズ戦でホーネッツでの今シーズン初出場を果たし、2年目のガードであるコン・クニュペルの復帰も間近と見られています。
articles.body:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- The Charlotte Hornets are getting healthy.

Coby White will make his season debut for the Hornets on Monday night when they host the Detroit Pistons, and shooting guard Kon Knueppel's return is "right around the corner," according to head coach Charles Lee.

Lee wouldn't give an exact date for Knueppel's return. Knueppel led the NBA in 3-pointers last season and finished as runner-up to Cooper Flagg in the NBA rookie of the year voting.

Both White (calf) and Knueppel (hamstring) were injured during offseason workouts and neither has played this season.

White became the team's starting point guard when the Hornets traded away LaMelo Ball earlier in the offseason. Dennis Schroder has been starting with White out.

Lee said White will be on a minutes restriction for the next few games.

Knueppel, who averaged 18.5 points and 5.3 rebounds last season, has been participating in 5-on-5 drills and the team has begun adding contact drills with him.

Knueppel is expected to take Sion James' spot in the starting lineup upon his return.

After Monday night's game, the Hornets visit Brooklyn on Wednesday night and host Boston on Thursday night.

articles.headline: Myles Garrett will return to practice this week for Los Angeles Rams
articles.description: Los Angeles Rams star pass rusher Myles Garrett, who has been on injured reserve since having arthroscopic knee surgery in mid-September, will return to practice this week, coach Sean McVay told reporters Monday.
articles.headlineJa: マイレス・ギャレットが今週、ロサンゼルス・ラムズの練習に復帰
articles.descriptionJa: ショーン・マクベイ監督は月曜日、9月中旬に膝の関節鏡視下手術を受けてから負傷者リストに入っていたロサンゼルス・ラムズのスターパスラッシャー、マイレス・ギャレットが今週練習に復帰することを記者団に明らかにしました。
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Los Angeles Rams star pass rusher Myles Garrett will return to practice this week, coach Sean McVay said.

Garrett has been on injured reserve since having arthroscopic knee surgery in mid-September. Garrett played in the Rams' season opener but said after the game that he was not 100% healthy. He sat out most of training camp while dealing with what McVay called knee irritation.

McVay said Monday that he did not want to put a timeline on when Garrett would be able to play in a game.

"I want to be careful to even set any sort of expectations," McVay said. "I think just taking it a day at a time is going to be the best way that we can approach it. Think that's the right thing for him, and really just to see how he responds. But I think it's a real positive that we're starting his clock."

Tight end Terrance Ferguson also could return to practice this week, McVay said. Ferguson has sat out the Rams' past five games on injured reserve after spraining his ankle in Week 3 against the Denver Broncos.

McVay said the Rams have not determined whether Ferguson will practice but said it is "it is looking more likely than not" that the Rams open the tight end's practice window.

McVay said the Rams will take it a day at a time with determining whether cornerbacks Jaylen Watson and Trent McDuffie will play Sunday against the Washington Commanders. Watson and McDuffie left the Rams' Week 8 victory because of injuries. McVay said Watson aggravated his previous right shoulder injury.

"We'll see what his status looks like as the week progresses," McVay said. "Came in, had some good strength, feeling good and optimistic, but we'll kind of take his status a day at a time and see where he's at by the time the game rolls around."

McDuffie, who left the game after taking a knee to his back, "came in feeling better than maybe what we expected," McVay said.

articles.headline: Wilbon taking leave of absence from ESPN to address health issues
articles.description: Michael Wilbon, the longtime ESPN commentator and co-host of "Pardon the Interruption," is taking a leave of absence to address health issues.
articles.headlineJa: ウィルボン、健康上の理由でESPNを休職
articles.descriptionJa: ESPNの長年のコメンテーターで「Pardon the Interruption」の共同ホストを務めるマイケル・ウィルボンが、健康上の問題を解決するため休職する。
articles.body:
Michael Wilbon is taking a break.

The longtime ESPN commentator and co-host of "Pardon the Interruption" alongside good friend Tony Kornheiser announced Monday he is taking a leave of absence because of what he described as "multiple health issues."

Wilbon, who turns 68 later this month, wrote in a post on X that he is taking a trip to "the injured list" but added he hopes it is "not an extended one."

While Wilbon, who is also featured on ESPN's NBA coverage, declined to go into full detail about what he is facing, he said during his weekly appearance Monday on Kornheiser's podcast "The Tony Kornheiser Show" that he is diabetic and that is "part of what I'm dealing with now, but not the entirety of it."

Wilbon's last appearance on "PTI," which last month celebrated its 25th anniversary and is credited with revolutionizing television's "sports debate" format, was on Oct. 26.

"I didn't do the show for a week because I was just exhausted," Wilbon told Kornheiser. "Beyond exhausted, lifeless. And this has been going on for a while."

Wilbon stressed that his decision is not a retirement and he plans to return at some point, adding that his symptoms became too significant to ignore.

"I have to listen," he said to Kornheiser. "I've got things going on that are forcing me to listen."

The show, in part, is a by-product of the friendship of Wilbon and Kornheiser, who became colleagues at The Washington Post in the 1980s.

"I have loved sparring and hosting PTI with Tony every single day these past 25 years," Wilbon wrote. "And I'm incredibly grateful for the support and encouragement of my colleagues as I take this time away to concentrate on me, especially my well-being."

articles.headline: Harbaugh reached out on Simmons trade, says Giants 'open for any call'
articles.description: John Harbaugh admitted to calling Titans owner Amy Adams Strunk about the since-traded Jeffery Simmons with New York open for business ahead of the deadline.
articles.headlineJa: ハーボー、シモンズのトレードについて接触、ジャイアンツは「あらゆる提案にオープン」と語る
articles.descriptionJa: ジョン・ハーボーは、その後トレードとなったジェフリー・シモンズについてタイタンズのオーナー、エイミー・アダムス・ストランクに電話したことを認めた。ニューヨーク（ジャイアンツ）は締め切りを前に交渉に意欲的だ。
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- New York Giants coach John Harbaugh said Monday they're not in any "secret society oath" and admitted to calling and leaving a voice message for Tennessee Titans owner Amy Adams Strunk about trading for star defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons.

Simmons was traded Thursday to the Chicago Bears for multiple first-round picks. The Giants had interest, which prompted Harbaugh to place the call.

"I did, I did," he said. "I left a message because you're turning over every stone, going to try everything. I mean, I'll put it out there, man. We're open for any call. Anybody who wants to call us or call anybody, call. Is there a song, there's a song like that. Call me, is it like that? Who sings that?"

It could be "Call Me Maybe" by Carly Rae Jepsen. Or "Call Me" by Blondie. But in any case, Harbaugh wasn't shy about making the call to an owner. He orbits at the ownership level and admittedly has better relationships with owners than general managers.

Harbaugh said people in the Giants organization make phone calls at every level. It's how they get information. It's how trades get done. They all know about the calls each other are making. They're doing what they believe is best for the Giants in a league where it's hard to get trades to the finish line.

"We're not part of any secret society oath that says you can only talk to somebody. We're not in that. We didn't get memo'd on that," Harbaugh said. "We're not in that agreement. So, like I said, anybody can call us. We won't be adhering to that particular agreement."

The Giants already expressed interest in Simmons. The interior of the defensive line is a need. They also have interest in Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, sources told ESPN. That also is expected to cost multiple high picks.

Running back is an area of need for the Giants, who flip-flopped starters in the past month. Cam Skattebo (hamstring) was working on the side with a trainer at Monday's practice, and Tyrone Tracy Jr. (hamstring) was recently placed on injured reserve.

The Giants players have heard about their interest in Simmons and Taylor, among others. They're not against such a move.

"It's a players' league," veteran offensive tackle Andrew Thomas said. "Anytime you have an opportunity to acquire whoever the player may be, the thought is that they'll help our team win. And our goal is to win games.

"So I'm never opposed to trying to figure out ways to have a better roster. They get paid the big bucks to make those decisions."

General manager Joe Schoen said last week that any move would have to make sense for the "short term and long term." Harbaugh reiterated that Monday.

"You want to have a short-term and a long-term win if you're going to do it with draft capital," he said.

The Giants are looking to add a significant player by the trade deadline Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. ET.

"Always, always. I mean, that's always the goal," Harbaugh said. "Easier said than done."

articles.headline: Cardinals' Mike LaFleur: Jeremiyah Love's injury to 'new portion' of his ankle
articles.description: Cardinals rookie running back Jeremiyah Love suffered a new ankle injury in Sunday's win over the Cowboys, coach Mike LaFleur said.
articles.headlineJa: カージナルスのマイク・ラフルール監督：ジェレマイア・ラブの怪我は足首の「別の箇所」
articles.descriptionJa: カージナルスのルーキーランニングバック、ジェレマイア・ラブが日曜日のカウボーイズ戦の勝利の中で、足首に新たな怪我を負ったとマイク・ラフルール監督が語った。
articles.body:
TEMPE, Ariz. -- Cardinals rookie running back Jeremiyah Love suffered a new ankle injury in Sunday's win over the Dallas Cowboys, coach Mike LaFleur said Monday.

LaFleur said Love's most recent ankle issue isn't related to Love's preseason or early-season ankle injuries, one of which happened to each ankle.

"It's a new portion of the ankle," LaFleur said. "So, I'll keep it at that."

Love walked off the field in the first half and slammed his helmet to ground on the sideline. After being looked at by trainers, he went into the blue injury tent and later walked to the locker room.

LaFleur said he had not talked to Love at the time of his news conference, so he didn't want to share more information, saying he would have more on Wednesday.

LaFleur also said wide receiver Kendrick Bourne's right ankle injury is "not good." A source told ESPN's Adam Schefter that Bourne has a fractured tibia that does not require surgery but will sideline him three months and end his season.

Running back Bam Knight is in the concussion protocol, said LaFleur, who added that he'll have more about left tackle Jayden Williams' knee injury on Wednesday.

LaFleur said wide receiver Reggie Virgil, who collided with the base of the goalpost in the fourth quarter and was carted off the field, is "great."

"The goalpost took the hit, not Reg," LaFleur said. "So, he had a smile on his face when he was laying there. That's just Reg."

articles.headline: Barry leads Everton to second win over Newcastle in four days
articles.description: Thierno Barry's second-half strike helped Everton return to winning ways in the Premier League with a 1-0 victory over Newcastle at St James' Park.
articles.headlineJa: バリーがリードし、エバートンが4日間で2度目のニューカッスル戦勝利を飾る
articles.descriptionJa: ティアノ・バリーが後半に決めたゴールにより、エバートンはセント・ジェームズ・パークでニューカッスルに1-0で勝利し、プレミアリーグで勝ち星を挙げた。
articles.body:
Thierno Barry's second-half strike helped Everton return to winning ways in the Premier League with a 1-0 victory over Newcastle United at St James' Park.

Following a first half lacking in clear-cut opportunities, the Toffees took the lead shortly after the restart when Barry stabbed home his fourth league goal of the campaign.

A frustrating night soured further for the Magpies as they finished the game with 10 men when substitute Jacob Ramsey was shown two yellow cards in quick succession at the death.

Everton ended a three-game winless run in the Premier League and moved up to seventh in the table, while Newcastle slipped to 13th.

Monday's match took place just four days after Everton's 3-1 win over Newcastle in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup and both sides made two changes to their starting XI as Anthony Elanga and Joelinton came in for the Magpies, while Jarrad Branthwaite and Harrison Armstrong lined up for the visitors.

Harvey Barnes looked lively on the left flank for the hosts, sending a curling shot wide before his looping cross floated narrowly past the far post and Jordan Pickford was forced to hold Will Osula's deflected cross from a tight angle.

Joelinton had an effort blocked by James Tarkowski and Merlin Röhl fired over the crossbar as both sides looked to break the deadlock.

James Garner blasted a free kick from the edge of the area straight into the Newcastle wall and Barnes was at the heart of the action again, firing in a dangerous cross which bounced off Branthwaite and was tipped over by Pickford.

Joelinton unleashed a fierce strike from distance which whizzed wide and Everton enjoyed a late flurry of chances before the break.

Jake O'Brien was unable to nod home Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall's cross and Harrison Armstrong skewed a first-time effort wide.

The Toffees picked up where they left off only four minutes into the second half when a slick pass from a free kick set Tyrique George free on the left to fire low at Lukás Hornícek.

His shot squeezed underneath the Newcastle goalkeeper, but Barry was quick to react to tap in the loose ball and the goal stood following a VAR check for two close offside calls.

Branthwaite's header was tipped away by Hornicek as the visitors looked to quickly double their advantage, while Fabian Schär hooked an effort over the crossbar and Pickford held Joe Willock's header.

Hornicek was then called into action at the opposite end to push away Dewsbury-Hall's strike and the Magpies goalkeeper made a solid low save from the resulting corner to deny O'Brien.

Barnes' cross from the left was nearly turned in by Elanga at the far post, but the ball hit the post and trickled across the goal-line before being cleared.

Newcastle looked to threaten around the Everton box as Pickford punched away Jacob Murphy's corner and the ball was recycled back to Ramsey, who dragged his volley narrowly wide.

articles.headline: Kane says new Bayern deal 'extremely close,' will happen in coming days
articles.description: Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane is determined to help Bayern Munich come through more difficult moments as they prepare to face Atlético Madrid in the Champions League.
articles.headlineJa: ケイン、バイエルンとの新契約は「極めて近い」とし、近日中に締結へ
articles.descriptionJa: バロンドール受賞者のハリー・ケインは、チャンピオンズリーグでアトレティコ・マドリードとの対戦を控える中、バイエルン・ミュンヘンが困難な局面を乗り越える手助けをしたいと決意している。
articles.body:
Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane expects to sign a new contract with Bayern Munich "within the next few days".

The England captain is heading towards the end of the four-year deal he agreed after leaving Tottenham Hotspur in the summer of 2023.

Kane scored 73 goals for club and country last season, winning two trophies in Germany and leading England to third place at the World Cup.

And the 33-year-old -- who last week was crowned the world's best player at a glittering ceremony in London -- is ready to extend his stay at the Allianz Arena.

"I would say it is more [a matter of] days," Kane said at a news conference ahead of Tuesday's Champions League match at Atlético Madrid. "There has been good conversations over this weekend and today as well.

"I know I keep saying we are close, but we are extremely close now. Details are just details in every contract.

"A lot of the bigger stuff has been ironed out and we are happy with, but in every contract there is loads of little things that go into it, small details that in the end the lawyers have to thrash out and figure out.

"So all in all I would say it is more days than weeks. From what I have heard, the conversations have gone well again today and hopefully we will be in a place to do something within the next few days."

Contract situation aside, Kane also said he is determined to help Bayern Munich come through more difficult moments the have faced this season and, in particular, the "rollercoaster ride" of the past week which saw him crowned the world's best player in London and then miss a penalty against Der Klassiker rivals Borussia Dortmund, in a 2-2 draw at the Allianz.

Bayern's selection problems deepened after the game, with midfielder Ismael Saibari facing a lengthy spell out after needing ankle surgery following his injury and forward Serge Gnabry having sustained a hamstring tear.

Assistant coach Aaron Danks will again take charge in Madrid on Tuesday night as Vincent Kompany continues his recovery at home after being diagnosed with meningeal irritation following his collapse during training.

Bayern will also check on Michael Olise and goalkeeper Manuel Neuer.

Olise picked up a knee problem late on against Dortmund, but trained on Monday. Neuer has also travelled to Spain as he looks to return from a foot injury.

Kane admits it has been a tough spell but one which he feels the Bayern squad can pull through together as they look to push on again following a 2-2 draw with Arsenal in their last European fixture.

"It has been a rollercoaster ride. We have experienced all sorts of emotions," Kane said at a news conference. "I had a fantastic moment winning the Ballon d'Or, but there were also the injuries and Joshua Kimmich's situation [earlier in the season] ... Those were difficult moments.

"You have to be able to cope with that, sport brings us together. We are missing key players and our coach too, but there are others who can seize this opportunity to show what they're made o

articles.headline: Jack Grealish, 'not match fit,' left out as Everton beat Newcastle again
articles.description: Jack Grealish was not named in Everton's squad for Monday's Premier League match at Newcastle United due to a fitness issue.
articles.body:
Jack Grealish was not named in Everton's squad for Monday's Premier League win over Newcastle United due to a fitness issue.

The 31-year-old was left out of the team for Thursday's Carabao Cup fourth-round meeting against the Magpies due to a breach of club discipline and Everton went on to win the game 3-1.

Both sides met again at St James' Park in the Premier League and Grealish was not included, with a starting lineup post on the Everton club website stating that he is "not match fit."

Everton went on to beat Newcastle for the second time in four days as Thierno Barry scored the game's only goal in a 1-0 win.

Grealish was also absent for the Toffees' 2-0 loss to Arsenal on Oct. 24, but that was put down to illness.

Providing an update on Grealish after the match, manager David Moyes said he is "not available yet."

Asked if there is a way back longer term, Moyes replied: "Of course there is, yeah."

The former Aston Villa midfielder is on a second consecutive season-long loan from Manchester City and has made six appearances for Everton this season.

During the last campaign, Grealish provided six assists and scored two goals in 20 appearances before suffering a season-ending foot injury in January.

He was not part of the England side that made a run to the semifinals of the World Cup before losing to Argentina.

Information from PA was used in this report.

articles.headline: Jaylen Brown's favorite purchase? An 18th century harp
articles.description: The Sixers guard's Boston apartment contains possession of some rare pieces.
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- 76ers forward Jaylen Brown -- who signed what was then the richest contract in NBA history three years ago -- said a golden harp in his Boston apartment is his most-cherished acquisition.

"I think my best, my most favorite purchase," Brown told Atlanta rapper Lil Baby in an interview last month.

Brown also discussed the prized possession in detail and gave a tour of his Boston apartment in an interview with Architectural Digest published Monday.

As tunes from his harp played in the background, Brown told Architectural Digest that it was made in the 18th century but that it was "reimagined" and is one of the most expensive pieces in his apartment.

He thanked his harpist, Li Shan Tan, the principal harp for the New Haven Symphony Orchestra, for being "an amazing therapist."

"Most of the time I use my harp, it's just me and my chef," Brown told Architectural Digest. "A memory raced through my head: me at the end of my 20s, with a harp [broken] in my unit. And how central it would be to the social hours of 10 p.m. to 4 a.m."

At times, Brown tries to play the harp himself.

"From time to time, when she is not around, I go and I try to re-create some sounds," Brown said.

The Boston Celtics chose Brown with the No. 3 pick in the 2016 draft. After 10 seasons and a championship in 2024, the Celtics traded Brown to Philadelphia this offseason for Paul George, two first-round picks (2028, 2031) and two second-round selections (2028, 2030).

"I grew up here age 19 to 29," Brown said. "I developed here in Boston as a young man.

"There's been other places, but this one -- I created it, it was crafted by my vision. This one felt the most like home."

Brown will play his former team Nov. 10 in Philadelphia.
